Knezevi Vinogradi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kneževi Vinogradi, Croatia

Not demolished. Kneževi Vinogradi, a Baranja village with roots to the Roman-era settlement of Donatium, was home to 37 families during Ottoman rule (recorded 1554) and later developed a winemaking economy under a mixed Hungarian, Croat, German, and Serb population (2,806 residents by 1910). The local Jewish community owned both a synagogue and this cemetery, established in 1888 (though earliest burials date to 1887); the community relocated to Osijek after WWI began, abandoning the synagogue, which was sold in 1948 and still stands today. The site was nationalized in 1947. Cemetery use continued through 1933.
